en: Just as before with the workflows, we'll
start with a visual
AI agent and we'll use N8N as a service that
allows us to create workflows and agents
visually.
Now, there are other services as well. And
of course, you can also follow along without
building anything.
If you want to follow along, you could sign
up with N8N.
They have a cloud offering where you would
be building your workflows and agents in
their cloud. And therefore they would also
offer hosting. So that you could immediately
share them with others, which is nice, but
you'd be paying for it. And that's not the
focus of this course. Instead, we'll use
another feature offered by n8n, which is to
run
a local server, which allows us to build and
run
AI workflows and agents with n8n locally.
And therefore, just as before in the
workflows section attached, you find a
starting project. For example, you'll need
the Node.js runtime installed on your
system. You'll also need an OpenAI API key
for this demo here. So that you can actually
send requests to a model in the cloud, to an
OpenAI model.
And regarding Node.js, you should visit
nodejs.org and then there head to the
download page and download it for your
operating system.
Just run these commands in your local
terminal or PowerShell.
That is what you should do to install
Node.js.
And for the OpenAI API key, you'll need an
OpenAI API account. And then there under API
keys, you need to create such a key and
we'll need that in a second.
And then you also find the instructions
regarding the commands you need to run in
your project to install all the dependencies
locally on your system of this project. And
for that, you should open a terminal,
navigate into your project folder. Here I'm
using Visual Studio Code, and if I open the
built-in terminal there, it's automatically
navigated into the folder. If you're using
an external terminal or PowerShell, you need
to navigate manually into the project folder
you downloaded.
And then just run these commands there
to install the dependencies and start the
local n8n server. You may see a few warnings
during installation. That is no problem. You
can ignore them. And this may also take a
while. And then after a while, the n8n
server will start up and you'll see an
address which you can visit in your browser
to see it there, or you should be able to
press O and you should keep that process up
and running as long as you are working with
your agent or if you wanna run it and you
can quit it with Ctrl+C if you're done. And
then restart it by running npm start again.
So I'll visit that address now and I'm now
on the n8n dashboard. Now when you run this
for the first time, you'll need to create an
account even though it's running locally.
You can enter any data you want there, but
you will need an account there
and then you'll need to sign in with that
account if you come back in the future. But
then you should see 3 workflows in there.
And again, if you wanna learn a bit more
about n8n, go back to that AI workflow
section where I give you a bit of a more
comprehensive introduction.
